macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound after sharp sell-off
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.1% to 24,579.42 and the S&P 500 gained 0.3% to 7,376.86, while the Dow fell 0.5% to 51,285.73. The rebound followed Thursday’s steep decline but did not prevent major weekly losses.[3]

items.title: Strong October jobs report boosts December Fed hike expectations
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. The data strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in December.[5][7]

items.title: Fed officials signal further tightening remains possible
items.summary: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the central bank is prepared to raise rates further if necessary, while emphasizing that policymakers need more information before deciding how much additional tightening is needed and when to act.[9]

items.title: Chip stocks recover as AI investment concerns persist
items.summary: Semiconductor shares rebounded, with AMD up 11.0%, Intel 7.7%, Micron 5.1% and Nvidia 2.8%. The recovery came after a broad sell-off driven by concerns about the cost and sustainability of the AI build-out.[9][6]

items.title: Global markets remain volatile amid AI valuation concerns
items.summary: Asian and European equities weakened, including a roughly 6% decline in Japan’s Nikkei 225 and a 1.9% fall in Germany’s DAX, as investors reassessed AI-related valuations and economic risks.[7]

items.title: Major technology and corporate developments add to market uncertainty
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly winding down an AI-computing rental arrangement with Oracle, Alphabet is taking over a Wyoming data-center project, Tesla is discontinuing the Cybertruck, and Anthropic’s IPO plans are facing valuation pressure after the market sell-off.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto markets tumble amid tech sell-off and regulatory uncertainty
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 3.2% to roughly $75,717 and Ether dropped 4.5% to about $2,238. Aggregate crypto liquidations reached approximately $1.22 billion in 24 hours, while XRP, BNB, and Solana also declined.[1]

items.title: U.S. Democrats consider broader crypto market-structure legislation
items.summary: House Democrats are reportedly discussing an expanded crypto bill that could increase SEC oversight, reduce the CFTC’s role, and add ethics restrictions for federal officials involved in crypto activities.[2]

items.title: China investigates halted Solana event in Shanghai
items.summary: Chinese authorities said they stopped Solana-related advertising and offline communications in Shanghai and will investigate the organizations and individuals involved, reiterating that domestic virtual-currency business activities are prohibited.[3]

items.title: Standard Chartered and SBI back crypto insurer Soter
items.summary: Standard Chartered’s SC Ventures and Japan’s SBI Group participated in a roughly $66 million Series B round for Soter Insure, which provides insurance for crypto-asset losses and plans to expand underwriting capacity.[3]

items.title: Hyperliquid-linked entity seeks U.S. approval for perpetual futures
items.summary: Hyperliquid Strategies filed to become a futures commission merchant, seeking approval to offer perpetual-futures markets to U.S. customers. HYPE fell about 8% over 24 hours amid the news.[4]

items.title: Bull Bitcoin adds default Payjoin support
items.summary: Bitcoin-focused exchange Bull Bitcoin announced integrated Payjoin deposits and withdrawals by default, aiming to provide stronger on-chain transaction privacy for users.[3]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA reportedly releases 25 classic PC games on Steam
items.summary: Electronic Arts reportedly added 25 older PC titles to Steam, GOG, and the EA app, including Ultima, Wing Commander, Crusader, and Theme Hospital. Seven titles received Anniversary Edition updates with restored video and technical improvements.

items.title: PlayStation cancels Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble
items.summary: PlayStation and developer Oh Bibi ended development of the mobile spin-off Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble. The game is scheduled for removal from mobile storefronts on November 21, with servers planned to remain available until May 1, 2027.

items.title: EA owners reportedly explore acquisition of Unity
items.summary: Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund and Silver Lake, which acquired Electronic Arts this year, are reportedly in early discussions to buy Unity at a potential valuation of about $25 billion. The talks may not result in a transaction.

items.title: GOG announces Linux launcher and preservation initiatives
items.summary: GOG reportedly announced that GOG Galaxy for Linux is in development, introduced the Retrovibe publishing label, and detailed additional classic-game preservation efforts during its first showcase.

items.title: Gears of War marks 20th anniversary with E-Day event
items.summary: The Coalition launched a two-week anniversary event in Gears of War: E-Day featuring limited-time modes, new rewards, and returning legacy content. A free General RAAM multiplayer skin is also planned.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day to revive legacy multiplayer content
items.summary: The Coalition is bringing back classic maps, modes, and skins in the second season of Gears of War: E-Day, alongside a new Horde mission and additional anniversary content.
